mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% in the month preceding the decision date reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing near-term S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 12 months of similar rate conditions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) suggest a labor market softening without cost-of-living pressures, which typically precedes a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% while CPIAUCSL decreases by >0.5% in the same month
regime_hint: labor market moderation with deflationary pressures
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns under such conditions are negative or flat, and the interaction coefficient (IC) is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in housing starts (HOUST) above 1,500K units in the prior month indicates strengthening building activity, which is associated with increased consumer confidence and higher equity valuations, driving positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite HOUST > 1,500K for at least 2 consecutive months (IC < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 102 (index) for three months signals supply-side weakness that can lead to a temporary S&P 500 decline over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 30-day average (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds +2% while the 3-month moving average of federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) remains below 4%, it indicates a shift toward inflationary expectations without aggressive policy tightening, which tends to produce positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly change > +2% and 3-month FEDFUNDS avg < 4%
regime_hint: inflation expectation rising in a loose policy environment
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative and the interaction IC is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) exceeding 200K in a month is interpreted as a labor market stress signal that typically precedes a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly lower than during the prior 6 months of similar claims spikes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (not directly observable in the provided proxies, but proxy via demand proxies like GDPC1) coupled with a decline in consumer confidence (not directly observable but assumed via external validation) create a forward-looking demand expansion signal that is expected to drive positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are flat or negative despite 2 consecutive months of GDPC1 growth (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of S&P 500 options put-call ratios (not directly observable but assumed as a proxy for fear) crosses above 0.6, it indicates elevated market stress that is associated with negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1) when the put-call ratio condition is met.
